where: Section 1 prose, Section 2 table, Worked example 1 (steps 1–5), quiz answers Q3 and Q7
problem: Exponents and integral limits are written flat, without superscript or subscript tags: "Σ c_n ejnω₀t", "e−2te−jωtdt", "∫0∞", "e−atu(t)", "e−j3ω". A student can read "e−2te−jωt" as "e minus 2t times e minus jωt" instead of e^(−2t)·e^(−jωt), and "e−atu(t)" is ambiguous.
fix: Use tags for every exponent and limit, as the main formula blocks already do: e<sup>jnω₀t</sup>, e<sup>−2t</sup>e<sup>−jωt</sup>, ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>∞</sup>, e<sup>−at</sup>u(t), e<sup>−j3ω</sup>.

problem: "At ω=0, Sa(0)=1" is not strictly true: Sa(y)=sin y/y is undefined at y=0. Only its limit is 1.
fix: Say "Sa(0) is the limit sin y/y as y→0, which is 1, so X(0)=2".

problem: "a short UPI confirmation burst needs more bandwidth than a steady carrier" compares a real pulse with a pure sinusoid. A steady carrier has exactly zero bandwidth, so the sentence invites the wrong picture that a carrier occupies some band.
fix: Compare two pulses instead: "...needs more bandwidth than a long, slowly varying burst."

problem: The note says the 1/2π "converts an ω integral to an f integral". The factor is not a converter; it makes the ω-form inverse consistent with the forward transform, and in the f-form it is cancelled by dω=2πdf.
fix: Write: "the 1/(2π) pairs with dω so that the round trip returns x(t); with ω=2πf and dω=2πdf it cancels, giving x(t)=∫X(f)e<sup>j2πft</sup>df."
